chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Zur'a, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about two men who had a slave girl between them, so they married her to a man. Then a man bought part of the two shares. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She becomes prohibited to him by his purchase of her, and that is that her sale is her divorce, unless he buys her from all of them entirely.'
ai.seo_question: What is the legal effect on a slave girl's marriage when one of her joint owners buys his share?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* elucidates the principle of *tamleek* (granting ownership) in the context of joint ownership (*syirkah*) of a slave girl, establishing that partial acquisition by one co-owner triggers an automatic divorce (*talaq*) for the wife. Scholars note this ruling highlights the legal interplay between property rights and marital status in classical fiqh, ensuring the husband's right to the wife is not fragmented. It underscores the Shia juristic view that the husband's entitlement is contingent upon the complete ownership of the slave by his side, preventing legal ambiguity in the marital bond.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Al Abbas Bin Marouf, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad, from Zurara, from Sama’at who said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about two men who had a slave girl between them, so they got her married to a man. Then the man bought part of their shares. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘She is Prohibited unto him by his stipulation of her, and that is that her sale is her divorce, unless he buys her from them entirely’.
